title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE OPENING OF AMRIT UDYAN SUMMER ANNUALS EDITION, 2026
subtitle: AMRIT UDYAN TO OPEN FOR THE PUBLIC FROM AUGUST 16 TO SEPTEMBER 15
body_text:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu graced the opening of Amrit Udyan Summer Annuals Edition, 2026 today (August 14, 2026).
The Summer Annuals of Amrit Udyan will be open for the public from August 16 to September 15, 2026. During that period, the Udyan will remain open from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, with the last entry at 5:00 PM. The Udyan will remain closed on all Mondays for maintenance.
Entry and exit for visitors will be from Gate No. 35, located near North Avenue Road. Entry to Amrit Udyan will be free of cost. Visitors have to book their slots online at visit.rashtrapatibhavan.gov.in advance. Booking of slots for a particular day will close at 10.00 AM on the previous day. There will be no on-the-spot booking available.
For the convenience of the visitors, drinking water stalls, First Aid posts, Rain Shelter and Restrooms will be set up along the route of the visit. A shuttle bus service with the banner ‘SHUTT LE SERVICE FOR AMRIT UDYAN’ will also be available from Central Secretariat Metro Station to the entry point to the Amrit Udyan at an interval of every 30 minutes between 9.30 AM and 6.00 PM.

enrichment.summary: President Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the Summer Annuals Edition 2026 of Amrit Udyan at Rashtrapati Bhavan on 14 August 2026. The garden will be open to the public free of cost from 16 August to 15 September 2026, between 10 AM and 6 PM (last entry 5 PM), closed on Mondays. Visitors must book slots online in advance via the Rashtrapati Bhavan website, with shuttle service available from Central Secretariat Metro Station.
enrichment.context: Amrit Udyan, formerly known as the Mughal Gardens, is the historic garden within the Rashtrapati Bhavan Estate in New Delhi, renamed in 2023 as part of the government's broader initiative to rename colonial-era and Mughal-associated landmarks with indigenous names reflecting India's 'Amrit Kaal' vision post-75 years of independence. The garden is periodically opened to the public during specific seasonal editions (like the Spring Festival and Summer Annuals), showcasing seasonal flowers and horticultural displays as part of Rashtrapati Bhavan's public outreach and heritage tourism efforts.
